label: Equivariant deterministic selection from supplied data
term: Equivariant deterministic selection from supplied data
definition: Equivariant t s f means f(t d)=s(f d) for every input datum d. The general obstruction separately assumes one datum is fixed, the two output candidates are swapped and distinct, and f selects one candidate. No bijectivity is required by the proof. Application to automorphisms requires an independently justified specification of ALL selector-relevant data; symmetry of psychology alone is insufficient. Deterministic total single-bearer outputs exclude optional abstention, random distributions and set-valued outputs from this theorem scope.
